content: Insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS-1) is a signaling adapter protein encoded by the IRS-1 gene in humans. It is a 131 kDa protein composed of 1242 amino acid residues. Structurally, it contains a pleckstrin homology (PH) domain at its N-terminus, followed by a phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) domain approximately 40 residues downstream, and a poorly conserved C-terminal tail. Together with IRS-2, IRS-3 (a pseudogene), and IRS-4, it shares homology with the Drosophila protein Chico, whose disruption has been shown to extend the median lifespan of flies by up to 48%. Similarly, IRS-1 mutant mice exhibit moderate lifespan extension and delayed onset of age-related pathologies. Function IRS-1 plays a critical role in transmitting signals from insulin and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) receptors to intracellular pathways, including the PI3K/Akt and Erk MAP kinase pathways. Upon tyrosine phosphorylation by the insulin receptor (IR), IRS-1 provides multiple binding sites for SH2 domain-containing proteins such as PI3K, Grb-2/Sos complexes, and SHP2. PI3K, when recruited by IRS-1, generates PIP3, which subsequently recruits Akt kinase. Akt is activated through phosphorylation at its T308 residue and analogous sites in PKC by PDK1. This phosphorylation is absent in tissues lacking IRS-1, and the signaling cascade ultimately leads to glucose uptake. The Grb-2/Sos complex, also known as RAS signaling, activates ERK1/2. In some tissues, IRS-1 signal transduction may be inhibited by SHP2. Tyrosine phosphorylation of insulin or IGF-1 receptors upon extracellular ligand binding induces cytoplasmic binding of IRS-1 to these receptors via its PTB domains. Multiple tyrosine residues on IRS-1 itself are then phosphorylated by these receptors, enabling IRS-1 to activate several signaling pathways, including PI3K and MAP kinase pathways. Alternative multi-site phosphorylation of serine/tyrosine residues in IRS-1 regulates insulin signaling both positively and negatively. The C-terminal region contains most of the phosphorylation sites of the protein. However, the C-terminal tail is unstructured, and the mechanisms by which phosphorylation regulates IRS-1 remain unclear. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα) has been shown to induce insulin resistance and multi-site serine/threonine phosphorylation, which blocks the interaction between IRS-1 and the juxtamembrane domain peptide, rendering IRS-1 inactive. Mice lacking IRS-1 exhibit only 50% of the body weight of normal mice. Regulation The cellular protein levels of IRS-1 are regulated by the Cullin 7 E3 ubiquitin ligase, which targets IRS-1 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation by the proteasome. Serine phosphorylation of IRS-1, induced by various molecules such as fatty acids, TNFα, and AMPK, has diverse effects on the protein, including cellular relocalization, conformational changes, and steric alterations. These processes lead to decreased tyrosine phosphorylation by insulin receptors and diminished PI3K recruitment. Collectively, these mechanisms promote IRS-1 degradation and insulin resistance. Other inhibitory pathways include SOCS proteins and O-linked glycosylation of IRS-1. SOCS proteins bind to insulin receptors and interfere with their phosphorylation of IRS-1, thereby attenuating insulin signaling. They can also bind to JAK, leading to reduced tyrosine phosphorylation of IRS-1. During hyperglycemia-induced insulin resistance, glucose accumulates in tissues as its hexosamine metabolite UDP-GlcNAc. High levels of this metabolite result in O-GlcNAc protein modifications. IRS-1 can undergo this modification, leading to its phosphorylation and functional suppression. Interactions IRS-1 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including Bcl-2, Grb-2, INSR, IGF1R, JAK1, JAK2, MAPK8, PIK3R1, PIK3R3, PTK2, PTPN11, PTPN1, and YWHAE. Role in Cancer As a signaling adapter protein, IRS-1 integrates various signaling cascades, suggesting its potential role in cancer progression. IRS-1 is implicated in multiple cancer types, including colorectal, lung, prostate, and breast cancer. It integrates signaling from insulin receptor (InsR), IGF-1 receptor (IGF1R), and other cytokine receptors and is elevated in β-catenin-induced cells. Evidence suggests that TCF/LEF-β-catenin complexes directly regulate IRS-1. IRS-1 is required for maintaining the neoplastic phenotype in adenomatous polyposis coli (APC)-mutated cells and for transformation in cells ectopically expressing oncogenic β-catenin. A dominant-negative mutant of IRS-1 functions as a tumor suppressor, whereas ectopic IRS-1 expression promotes oncogenic transformation. IRS-1 is upregulated in colorectal cancers (CRC) with elevated levels of β-catenin, c-MYC, InsRβ, and IGF1R and promotes CRC metastasis to the liver. Reduced apoptosis of crypt stem cells is associated with colon cancer risk. In APC (min/+) mutated mice, reduced IRS-1 expression increases radiation-induced apoptosis in crypt cells. Partial or complete IRS-1 deficiency in APC (min/+) mice results in fewer tumors compared to IRS-1 (wild-type) APC (min/+) mice. In lung adenocarcinoma cell line A549, IRS-1 overexpression reduces growth. Tumor-infiltrating neutrophils have been implicated in modulating tumor growth and invasiveness. Neutrophil elastase degrades IRS-1 by accessing the endosomal compartment of carcinoma cells. IRS-1 degradation induces cell proliferation in mouse and human adenocarcinomas. Ablation of IRS-1 alters downstream signaling through PI3K, increasing its interaction with platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR). Thus, IRS-1 acts as a major regulator of PI3K in lung adenocarcinoma. Evidence also suggests a role for IRS-1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In a rat model, focal overexpression of IRS-1 is associated with early events in hepatocarcinogenesis. During the progression of preneoplastic foci into HCC, IRS-1 expression gradually decreases, reflecting a metabolic shift toward a malignant neoplastic phenotype. Transgenic mice co-expressing IRS-1 and hepatitis Bx (HBx) protein exhibit a higher rate of hepatocellular dysplasia, leading to HCC development. However, IRS-1 or HBx expression alone is insufficient to induce neoplastic alterations in the liver. Their combined expression activates IN/IRS-1/MAPK and Wnt/β-catenin cascades, driving HCC transformation. In LNCaP prostate cancer cells, ectopic IRS-1 expression increases cell adhesion and reduces cell motility via an IGF-1-independent mechanism mediated by PI3K. Unconventional phosphorylation of serine 612 by PI3K in IRS-1 is due to hyperactivation of the Akt/PKB pathway in LNCaP cells. IRS-1 interacts with integrin α5β1, activating an alternative signaling cascade that decreases cell motility, opposing the IGF-1-dependent mechanism. Loss of IRS-1 expression and PTEN mutations in LNCaP cells may promote metastasis. Ex vivo studies of IRS-1 in prostate cancer show ambiguous results. Downregulation of IGF1R in bone marrow biopsies of metastatic prostate cancer correlates with reduced IRS-1 expression and significant PTEN reduction in 3 out of 12 cases. Most tumors continue to express IRS-1 and IGF1R during metastatic disease progression. IRS-1 plays a functional role in breast cancer progression and metastasis. Overexpression of PTEN in MCF-7 epithelial breast cancer cells inhibits cell growth by suppressing the MAPK pathway. ERK phosphorylation through the IRS-1/Grb-2/Sos pathway is inhibited by PTEN's phosphatase activity. PTEN does not affect IRS-1-independent MAPK activation. When treated with insulin, ectopic PTEN expression in MCF-7 cells suppresses IRS-1/Grb-2/Sos complex formation due to differential IRS-1 phosphorylation. IRS-1 overexpression has been linked to antiestrogen resistance and hormone independence in breast cancer. Tamoxifen (TAM) inhibits IRS-1 function, suppressing the IRS-1/PI3K signaling cascade in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) MCF-7 cells. IRS-1 siRNA reduces IRS-1 transcript levels, thereby decreasing protein expression in MCF-7 ER+ cells. Reduced IRS-1 expression decreases cell survival, and siRNA treatment effects are additive to TAM treatment effects. IGFRs and estrogen coaction facilitate growth in various breast cancer cell lines. However, amplification of IGF1R signaling can eliminate the need for estrogen in the transformation and growth of MCF-7 cells. IRS-1 overexpression in breast cancer cells reduces estrogen requirements, and this reduction depends on IRS-1 levels in the cells. Estradiol enhances IRS-1 expression and the activity of ERK1/2 and PI3K/Akt pathways in MCF-7 and CHO cells transfected with the mouse IRS-1 promoter. Estradiol acts directly on IRS-1 regulatory sequences and positively regulates IRS-1 mRNA production. Reduced anchorage-dependent/independent cell growth and initiation of cell death under low growth factor and estrogen conditions are observed in MCF-7 cells with downregulated IRS-1. miR-126 is underexpressed in breast cancer cells and targets IRS-1 at the transcriptional level, inhibiting the G1/G0 to S phase transition during the cell cycle in HEK293 and MCF-7 cells. Tumors demonstrate squamous differentiation associated with the β-catenin pathway. IRS-1 interacts with β-catenin both in vitro and in vivo. IRS-1 and its homologue IRS-2 play distinct roles in breast cancer progression and metastasis. Overexpression of either is sufficient to cause tumorigenesis in vivo. Lung metastasis frequency is elevated in IRS-1-deficient tumors but decreased in IRS-2-deficient tumors. IRS-2 positively impacts breast cancer metastasis, whereas stronger metastatic potential is observed when IRS-1 is downregulated. IRS-1 is strongly expressed in ductal carcinoma in situ, while IRS-2 is elevated in invasive tumors. Therefore, IRS-1 may serve as a useful marker for evaluating the effectiveness of specific drug therapies in breast cancer treatment.
